 JUDGMENT As these six appeals are arising out of common judgment and award of the Tribunal, they are heard together and disposed of by this common judgment. 
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petitions before the Tribunal. 
3. MFA No.3421/2017, MFA No.3423/17 and MFA No.3424/17 are filed by the Insurer of the offending vehicle seeking reduction of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal. MFA No.4317/17,
MFA 4318/17 and MFA 4319/17 are filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal. The details are shown in the tabular column as below:

The Tribunal has awarded compensation in MVC No.509/16 against which the Insurance Company has filed MFA No.3421/2017 contending that claimant Nos. 5 and 6 are married daughters of deceased Ramaiah and thus, the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 Tribunal has erred in awarding compensation to them under `loss of estate'
applying the multiplier system as in the case of loss of dependency at Rs.3,50,000/-. 
5. In MVC No.510/2016 against which MFA No.3423/2018 is filed by the Insurer, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.30,96,160/- in favour of claimants 1 to 4 who are wife and children of deceased Ganesh, whereas, in MVC No.511/2016 against which MFA No.3424/2017, the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.1,70,000/- in favour of Mater Manoj-claimant/injured.

10 6. MVC No.509/2016 was filed by Claimant No.5 Nagamma and claimant No.6 Anitha on account of death of their father Ramaiah and MVC No.510/2016 was filed by claimants being the wife and children of deceased Ganesh. MVC No.511/2016 was filed by claimant himself i.e. Master Manoj who sustained injuries on account accident that occurred on 28.12.2015. 
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 7. The brief and relevant facts of the case of the claimants are as under:
On 28.12.2015 at about 4.30 p.m. when the deceased Ganesh was riding Bajaj Chetak Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-S-6889 and his father Ramaiah was pillion rider along with his sister's minor son Master Manoj who were proceeding from Channena Agrahara to Anekal on account of ill-health of minor child- Manoj. When they were proceeding to Anekal near, Samandur Gate on Anekal-Hosur Road at that time, a bus bearing Regn.No.KA-01-C-3311 came from opposite direction from Anekal to Hosur in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle which Ganesh was riding. As a result, Ganesh, Ramaiah and Master Manoj fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 
8. Immediately after the accident, the injured were shifted to Government Hospital, Anekal. But, the doctors declared Ganesh and Ramaiah brought dead and given - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 treatment to Master Manoj who sustained injuries in the accident. 
9. The claimants filed petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 on the ground that the claimant nos.5 and 6 are none other than the daughters of deceased Ramaiah and the claimants in MVC No.510/2016 contended that claimant no.1 is wife of Ganesh, claimant nos. 2 and 3 are his daughters and claimant no.4 is the son of Ganesh.
10. The claimants have taken a contention that Ramaiah was aged about 58 years and was doing coolie work and also the milk vending business and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month. In MVC 510/2016, the claimants contended that Ganesh was aged about 36 years and he was working as driver in Madhura Garments, Marasur Gate, and earning Rs.15,000/- per month. 
11. On account of untimely death of Ramaiah and Ganesh, claimants in MVC No.509/2016 lost their father,
- 15 - The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Master Manoj C on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56676281/
11 NC: 2024:KHC:16193 claimant no.1 in 510/2016 lost her husband and claimant nos. 2 to 4 have lost their father.
12. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the claimants and respondent no.2-Insurance Company and perused the judgment and award of the tribunal. 
13. As there is no dispute regarding the death of deceased Ramaiah, Ganesh and the injuries sustained by Manoj in the road traffic accident that occurred on 28.12.2015, since the Insurance Company has taken contention that there was contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and therefore the liability should also be fastened on the insurer of the rider of the motor cycle, the points which arise for consideration in these appeals are:
i) Whether Appellant/respondent no.2- Insurance Company prove that accident occurred on account of negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle?
- 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 ii) Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or it calls for interference? Re. Point No.1: 
14 . Learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that, the rider and pillion rider were majors who were succumbed to the injuries and the injured Boy Manoj was aged 14 years as on the date of accident. The rider of the motor cycle knew that he was riding Bajaj Chetak Scooter which was involved in the accident which is meant only for two adults and in extreme circumstances, a child could be accommodated. 
Considering the capacity of the vehicle, three grown up adults could not have traveled on Bajaj Chetak Scooter. That itself is sufficient ground for cause of accident. 
When somebody is traveling on a small vehicle with more number of persons, that itself is a detriment to the rider to ride the vehicle smoothly by following all the traffic rules. Therefore, in the fact situation, when the rider of the motorcycle has taken responsibility of taking two pillion riders on such a small vehicle, the rider of the vehicle should have been more cautious - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 in riding the motor cycle. It is needless to say that the accident took place in such a way that all the three persons on the scooter were grievously injured and out of them two were succumbed to the injuries. 
The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Master Manoj C on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56676281/
12 15. Therefore, the learned counsel contended that inspite of the fact that they knew about it that they have travelled on the said motorcycle putting their life into risk as well as the life of other road users to the risk, whereby, contributing to the cause of accident, have caused accident which is a matter of serious concerned. 
16. Further, it is contended that, the very rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle itself is an offence which is punishable under the provisions of MV Act, inasmuch as,
more than two persons travelling on the motorcycle, not being permissible. In that view of the matter, the rider and pillion rider on the aforesaid scooter at that point of time were tort feasers. 
When they were tort feasers, question of seeking compensation does not arise. The Tribunal ought to have considered these factual and legal aspects of the matter and should have dismissed the claim petition. 
- 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 17. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company relied upon the judgment of co-ordinate Bench in MFA 101508/2014 dated 5.7.2023 and MFA No.25390/2011 and connected matters disposed of on 7.4.2017.
18. A perusal of the evidence on record i.e. P.W.1 and 2 are not eye witnesses to the accident. 
However, PW.3 alone is an eye witness to the accident. As per the oral testimony of PW.3, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the bus, which came on extreme wrong side of the road i.e. towards extreme right and dashed to the motor cycle on which said deceased Ramaiah, Ganesh and Master Manoj were traveling, while overtaking a matador. 
19. In the cross-examination of PW.3 nothing worth has been elicited from his testimony to discredit his contention. From a perusal of FIR and complaint, it appears that the accident occurred on 28.12.2015 at 4.30 p.m. As per the contents of FIR and complaint, it appears that the offending bus came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the - 19 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 scooter in which these two deceased persons along with minor child Manoj were proceeding. 
20. From a perusal of contents of Ex.P28 charge sheet, the IO investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the driver of the bus. The Insurance Company has not challenged the charge sheet in material particulars. As per Ex.P6, IMV report, the bus bearing Registration No.KA-01-C- 3311 got damaged i.e. front wind glasses were damaged right side glass also damaged. 
21. From a perusal of IMV report, motor cycle front wheel nudged and the only front tires were damaged. But, from the perusal of the contents of spot Mahazr, no where it is seen, the driver of bus The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Master Manoj C on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56676281/
13 had applied the brake, it clearly establishes that the driver of the bus was in a high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life. 
22. Admittedly, the deceased Ganesh and Ramaiah were traveling in a motor cycle in order to take Manoj to the hospital for treatment on extreme urgency. The fact that the deceased was riding the motor cycle along with two pillion riders may not - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 by itself make him guilty of contributory negligence, but, at the most, he could make guilty of him of violating the law. 
23. Sec.128 of MV Act, 1988 imposes a restriction on the rider of two wheeler - motor cycle not to carry more than one person as pillion. Sec.194-C inserted by amendment Act of 32 of 2019 prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle riders and pillion riders. 
Therefore, the fact that a person was pillion rider on motor cycle along with the rider and one more person on pillion, may be a violation of the law, but, such violation by itself cannot lead to contributory negligence unless it is established that the very act of riding along with other two persons has contributed either for causing accident or the impact of the accident upon the victim. 
24. There must either be casual connect between the violation and the accident or that casual connect between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim, whereas, in the instant case, the investigating officer made the driver of the bus as accused. 
- 21 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 25. In order to establish the contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle,
respondent no.2 - Insurance Company has not examined the driver of the bus. In order to ascertain the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, as per the contents of spot Mahazar, the accident occurred on the extreme right side of the road. It shows that the driver of the bus took the bus to the extreme right side. Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of the deceased rider contributed either to the accident or nature of the injuries sustained, the rider cannot be held guilty of contributory negligence. Therefore, there is no merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company so as to fasten contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle. in MFA No.3421/2017 (MVC No.509/2016):
26. In this appeal filed by Insurance Company the claimants 1 to 4 are wife and children of deceased Ganesh and claimants Nos.5 and 6 are the daughters of deceased Ramaiah. But, this appeal is confined only to the claim of claimant nos. 5 - 22 - The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Master Manoj C on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56676281/
14 NC: 2024:KHC:16193 and 6. The claimants, in order to prove their case have examined claimant no.1 wife of deceased Ganesh speaking for other claimants along with other two witnesses PWs. 2 and 3 and got marked Exhibits Ex.P1 to P31. One Dr.Prakashappa is also examined as PW.4 speaking for injuries of Master Manoj. 
27. The very fact that the deceased was proceeding towards Anekal town in order to show the ill boy Master Manoj to the Doctor at Anekal Hospital in a high speed by its rider and as a result, the claimants have stated that Ramaiah and Ganesh sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries and in the accident, said Manoj also sustained grievous injuries. The claimants in MVC No.509/2016 have stated that at the time of accident, the deceased Ramaiah was aged 58 years and was doing coolie and also milk vending business. In this regard, apart from adducing oral evidence,
have got examined Smt.Nagamma, the daughter of deceased Ramaiah as PW.2 and spoken about avocation of their father. The claimant nos. 5 and 6 are his daughters. Though claimants are daughters of Ramaiah, they are married. They are not dependent upon the income of their father. 
Thus, they are not entitled to - 23 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 compensation under the head `loss of dependency'. However, they are entitled to compensation under the head `loss of estate'. Thus, considering the age of deceased Ramaiah as 58 years, the year of accident 2015 and his avocation as coolie, his income is assessed at Rs.9,000/- per month. No contra evidence is placed by respondent-Insurer in this regard.

annotations.text: 22. Admittedly, the deceased Ganesh and Ramaiah were traveling in a motor cycle in order to take Manoj to the hospital for treatment on extreme urgency.

The fact that the deceased was riding the motor cycle along with two pillion riders may not - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 by itself make him guilty of contributory negligence, but, at the most, he could make guilty of him of violating the law.
23. Sec.128 of MV Act, 1988 imposes a restriction on the rider of two wheeler - motor cycle not to carry more than one person as pillion.
Sec.194-C inserted by amendment Act of 32 of 2019 prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle riders and pillion riders.

Therefore, the fact that a person was pillion rider on motor cycle along with the rider and one more person on pillion, may be a violation of the law, but, such violation by itself cannot lead to contributory negligence unless it is established that the very act of riding along with other two persons has contributed either for causing accident or the impact of the accident upon the victim.

24. There must either be casual connect between the violation and the accident or that casual connect between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim, whereas, in the instant case, the investigating officer made the driver of the bus as accused.

In order to establish the contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle,
respondent no.2 - Insurance Company has not examined the driver of the bus.
In order to ascertain the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, as per the contents of spot Mahazar, the accident occurred on the extreme right side of the road.
It shows that the driver of the bus took the bus to the extreme right side.

Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of the deceased rider contributed either to the accident or nature of the injuries sustained, the rider cannot be held guilty of contributory negligence.

i) Whether Appellant/respondent no.2- Insurance Company prove that accident occurred on account of negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle?

summary.arguments:
The rider of the motor cycle knew that he was riding Bajaj Chetak Scooter which was involved in the accident which is meant only for two adults and in extreme circumstances, a child could be accommodated.

Considering the capacity of the vehicle, three grown up adults could not have traveled on Bajaj Chetak Scooter.
That itself is sufficient ground for cause of accident.

When somebody is traveling on a small vehicle with more number of persons, that itself is a detriment to the rider to ride the vehicle smoothly by following all the traffic rules.
Therefore, in the fact situation, when the rider of the motorcycle has taken responsibility of taking two pillion riders on such a small vehicle, the rider of the vehicle should have been more cautious - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 in riding the motor cycle.
16. Further, it is contended that, the very rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle itself is an offence which is punishable under the provisions of MV Act, inasmuch as,
more than two persons travelling on the motorcycle, not being permissible.
summary.ANALYSIS:
The fact that the deceased was riding the motor cycle along with two pillion riders may not - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 by itself make him guilty of contributory negligence, but, at the most, he could make guilty of him of violating the law.

23. Sec.128 of MV Act, 1988 imposes a restriction on the rider of two wheeler - motor cycle not to carry more than one person as pillion.

Therefore, the fact that a person was pillion rider on motor cycle along with the rider and one more person on pillion, may be a violation of the law, but, such violation by itself cannot lead to contributory negligence unless it is established that the very act of riding along with other two persons has contributed either for causing accident or the impact of the accident upon the victim.
24. There must either be casual connect between the violation and the accident or that casual connect between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim, whereas, in the instant case, the investigating officer made the driver of the bus as accused.
In order to establish the contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle,
respondent no.2 - Insurance Company has not examined the driver of the bus.
It shows that the driver of the bus took the bus to the extreme right side.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of the deceased rider contributed either to the accident or nature of the injuries sustained, the rider cannot be held guilty of contributory negligence.
However, they are entitled to compensation under the head `loss of estate'.
